title: AWS CWI Exam Prep in Savannah, GA: 6-Day Course
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for Savannah aerospace, port crane, bridge, auto supplier and turbine plant inspectors: Part C code choice, Part B and eligibility.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Preparation in Savannah: Six Days for Coastal Georgia Aerospace, Port, Bridge and Manufacturing Welding Inspectors
html:
Savannah's economy is built on three very different kinds of metalwork. Gulfstream Aerospace, the largest private employer in the metro area, makes business jets on a campus around the city's airport. The Georgia Ports Authority is close to finishing a rebuild of Ocean Terminal, two miles downriver from Garden City, the country's third-busiest container terminal. And west of the city, Hyundai's Metaplant in Bryan County and a planned Mitsubishi Power expansion near Pooler are adding vehicle and gas turbine manufacturing. Each sector welds to different rules, and each needs people who can tell an acceptable weld from a rejectable one and prove it on paper.

Atlantis NDT's six-day course prepares coastal Georgia candidates for the AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination: welders and fitters stepping into quality roles, crane and terminal maintenance staff, supplier QC technicians, NDT technicians and manufacturing engineers. Only the American Welding Society can administer the examination and issue the certification; each candidate applies to AWS separately and has to meet its eligibility and vision rules in person. AWS has not approved or endorsed this course, and Atlantis has no sight of AWS examination content. There is no Atlantis classroom in Savannah. Candidates can work through the six days online at their own pace with an instructor answering questions, an employer can have them delivered at its facility for a group, or a single candidate can book one-to-one sessions, online or in person at a location agreed when booking. Each day of the outline is described on the AWS CWI exam prep page.

Savannah's welding work at a glance

Employer or projectWhat the latest reports sayWhere a CWI fitsPart C book that usually fits
Gulfstream AerospaceMore than 13,000 employees in coastal Georgia; G500 and G600 manufactured in Savannah, on a campus of nearly 500 acres (AJC, May 2026)Aerospace suppliers, tooling and ground equipment shops, maintenance and facilities workAWS D17.1 for aerospace fusion welding; D1.1 for structures
Ocean Terminal, Georgia Ports AuthorityWharf of 2,650 feet complete, eight ship-to-shore cranes on site since January 2025, full reopening expected in late 2028Crane, wharf and terminal steel during construction and maintenanceAWS D1.1
Talmadge Memorial Bridge, Georgia DOTCable replacement and a study of raising the deck in final design, with procurement due to be finalized in late 2026Bridge fabrication, rehabilitation and owner inspectionAWS D1.5
Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America, Bryan CountyAbout 4,420 people across eight companies on site in October 2026Supplier QC, tooling, maintenance and plant construction contractorsAWS D1.1
Mitsubishi Power, near PoolerExpansion announced in October 2026 to make gas turbine parts, with more than 220 new jobsManufacturing quality roles and the contractors who build and equip the plantAWS D1.1 or the ASME option, by role

The right-hand column is a starting point. The contract, drawing or customer specification always decides which document governs a weld, and many Savannah employers add their own standards on top.

Aerospace welding and the D17.1 option

The AJC reported in May 2026 that Gulfstream builds its G500 and G600 lines in Savannah, brought wing manufacturing in-house in 2014 and uses robotics on new purpose-built production lines, and that its presence has drawn suppliers to the area. Much of an airframe is machined, formed and fastened rather than welded, but fusion welding still appears in aerospace hardware, tooling and the equipment that supports production and maintenance. When a candidate's job is fusion welding of aerospace parts, AWS D17.1, Specification for Fusion Welding for Aerospace Applications, is the Part C book written for it; AWS listed the 2024 edition for the exam in November 2026. D17.1 sorts welds into classes according to how critical the part is, and the acceptance criteria tighten as the class rises, so Part C practice in that book is largely about finding the right class and the right table quickly.

Aerospace customers usually flow down their own requirements for welding and for the people who inspect it, and those requirements take precedence over any general credential. Treat the CWI as proof of broad welding knowledge, then learn the customer specifications that apply to your shop. For NDT in this sector, see aerospace NDT training in Savannah.

Ocean Terminal, Garden City and the cranes

The Georgia Ports Authority's overhaul of Ocean Terminal, a 200-acre cargo facility on the Savannah River, involved near-total demolition, a rebuilt and reinforced wharf, new truck gates and an overpass, new buildings and an upgraded container yard. The AJC reported in September 2026 that the 2,650-foot wharf was complete, that the first phase of container yard work was due in summer 2027 and that the terminal should fully reopen in late 2028, when its yearly capacity would rise from 200,000 to 1.75 million container units. Its eight blue ship-to-shore cranes, each more than 200 feet tall, arrived in January 2025. Until the yard work is finished, the terminal serves as a lay berth for vessels waiting for space at Garden City, which had already moved more than one million container units in the fiscal year that began on July 1, 2026.

Container cranes, crane rails, wharf fittings and terminal structures are welded steel, and building, maintaining and modifying them keeps structural welders and inspectors busy at both terminals. That work is normally done to AWS D1.1 or the crane maker's specifications, which makes D1.1 the natural Part C choice for port maintenance and terminal construction crews. Reading: AWS D1.1 and D1.1 weld acceptance criteria.

Talmadge Bridge maintenance

Georgia DOT began single-lane closures on the Talmadge Memorial Bridge in September 2026 for its major maintenance project. WTOC reported that the fourth work package of the US 17/SR 404 Spur Bridge Major Maintenance Project covers replacing the bridge's cables and studying whether shortening them could raise the deck, giving more clearance for larger container ships; that package was in final design, with procurement expected to be finalized in the fourth quarter of 2026. Rehabilitation work on a large bridge brings steel repairs, replacement components and new attachments, generally fabricated and welded to AWS D1.5, the Bridge Welding Code, under the owner's specifications. Inspectors who want bridge work should weigh D1.5 for Part C; background is at AWS D1.5.

A car plant and its suppliers in Bryan County

About 4,420 people worked across eight companies at Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in October 2026, roughly 2,200 of them hired directly by the plant, against a target of 8,500 by 2031. The site builds the Ioniq 5 and Ioniq 9 electric vehicles and the Kia Sportage hybrid. Vehicle bodies are joined mostly by robots and resistance welding, so the arc welding inspection work tends to sit with the suppliers that make frames, brackets and subassemblies, with tooling and fixture builders, and with the contractors who build and maintain the plant's structures and equipment. In those roles a CWI is usually measuring weld size, profile and position against a drawing and the customer's weld standard, and AWS D1.1 is the common reference code.

Gas turbine parts near Pooler

On October 23, 2026 Georgia's governor announced that Mitsubishi Power would expand its Savannah Machinery Works at 1000 Pine Meadow Drive near Pooler, in Chatham County, to manufacture parts for gas turbines, adding more than 220 jobs in manufacturing, operations, heavy machinery and technician roles. A groundbreaking was still to be scheduled. Turbine component manufacturing runs to the maker's own specifications and quality system, while the construction of a new plant brings steel erection, process and utility piping, and equipment installation. A CWI could fit either side, choosing D1.1 for the structural work or the ASME option, Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, for a career in pressure piping.

Savannah Tech and the AWS Atlanta Section

Savannah Technical College offers a Welding and Joining diploma and seven certificates, among them basic and advanced shielded metal arc, flux cored arc, gas metal arc, gas tungsten arc, vertical shielded metal arc and Master Welder I. Classes run at the Savannah, Liberty and Effingham campuses and at several high school sites including Bryan County High School, with night and weekend options and a focus on passing code welding tests. A completed diploma of this kind usually places a candidate on the trade or vocational line of the AWS experience table, though AWS has the final word.

The college's AWS student chapter, known as the Southern Welders, belongs to the AWS Atlanta Section. Savannah candidates looking for section meetings should check the Atlanta Section's notices and use the section finder on aws.org for anything closer to the coast.

Working backward from a Part B date

Part B is the practical, run by AWS at its seminar locations; Parts A and C are computer-based tests at Prometric centers. Georgia's entry on the AWS list of CWI training locations in late 2026 was Kennesaw, northwest of Atlanta, and Tampa, Miami and Norfolk also appeared on the list. Plan from the practical backward:

  1. Choose a Part B session on the AWS seminar and exam schedule that avoids vessel peaks, model launches or plant start-ups.
  2. Submit the AWS application no later than six weeks before that date, the US deadline.
  3. Before applying, collect proof of education, a job-by-job experience record with people who can confirm it, and a passed vision test on the AWS visual acuity form.
  4. Start the six days of study before you apply, so the fundamentals are done by the time AWS reviews the application.
  5. Once accepted, book Parts A and C with Prometric using the eligibility code in your AWS confirmation, following the order and window AWS sets.
  6. Spend the last stretch on timed practice papers and gauge work, since every part needs at least 72 percent.

The practical asks 46 questions about specimens, tools and documents AWS supplies, so practise measuring fillet legs, reinforcement, undercut and misalignment until the readings come without hesitation. Kennesaw keeps the trip inside Georgia for most Savannah candidates, although a Florida or Virginia session may suit someone whose work calendar is clearer at a different time of year. The CWI exam cost calculator helps you price the trip.

Three Savannah backgrounds and how they line up

Hypothetical backgroundAWS experience lineWhat to document
Savannah Tech Welding and Joining diploma, then four years of structural and pipe welding at a fabricatorTrade or vocational courses: four yearsEach employer's dates, processes, materials and codes, and any welder qualification tests, with a supervisor to confirm them
High school diploma and six years as a maintenance welder on port cranes and terminal equipmentHigh school diploma: five yearsStructural repairs, the procedures followed and any inspection or record-keeping duties
Associate degree in engineering technology and three years as a quality technician checking welded assemblies at an automotive supplierAssociate degree or higher: two yearsEvidence that the inspection work was welding-related, which AWS decides

Candidates short of the CWI thresholds can look at the AWS Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI), which has lower experience requirements. The CWI requirements guide explains the rules in more detail.

A group course at a Savannah facility

A terminal contractor, fabricator or automotive supplier with several candidates can host the six days at its own facility. The group practises on its own weld samples and gauges, and code sessions follow the book most of them will take, often D1.1 around the port and plants. Because the employer sets the weeks, the course can be placed around vessel schedules, model launches or a plant's commissioning dates. Each person still applies to AWS individually, with their own vision record and experience evidence.

Individual candidates working terminal rotations or plant shifts often prefer to study online. The six days of material become a study plan you can stretch across several weeks of evenings and days off, with the instructor answering written questions as you go and timed practice papers to show when you are ready. If a single weak area, such as welding symbols or the code book, keeps pulling practice scores down, the one-to-one format lets you spend dedicated sessions on it with the instructor, online or in person.

After certification

A CWI stays valid for nine years, with renewal paperwork due at years three and six and recertification at year nine through professional development hours, a repeat of Part B, or the AWS Certified Radiographic Interpreter credential. Many coastal Georgia CWIs add NDT methods, which the employer certifies under its written practice; Atlantis provides training based on ASNT SNT-TC-1A, such as VT Level 2, MT Level 2, PT Level 2 and UT Level 2, with the employer certifying afterward.

Local pages: NDT training in Savannah, magnetic particle testing in Savannah, ultrasonic testing in Savannah, and CWI exam prep in Jacksonville, North Charleston and Atlanta.

Contacting Atlantis from Savannah

Say which format you prefer, how many candidates need preparation, the code book each plans to use for Part C and the Part B session you are aiming at. Employers should add the facility address and the weeks that fit around operations. If an experience record looks marginal, outline it and we will list what to confirm with AWS before you apply. Quotes for each format are prepared on request, and we reply within one business day.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis classroom in Savannah?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Savannah. The course runs online at your own pace, at an employer's facility for a group, or one-to-one, online or in person at a location agreed when booking.

faq.q: Can an aerospace welder use AWS D17.1 for Part C?
faq.a: Yes. AWS D17.1, Specification for Fusion Welding for Aerospace Applications, is on the AWS list of Part C books, and in November 2026 AWS named the 2024 edition. Customer specifications still govern the welds at your workplace.

faq.q: Where is the nearest Part B site to Savannah?
faq.a: The AWS list of CWI training locations in late 2026 included Kennesaw, Georgia, northwest of Atlanta, along with Tampa, Miami and Norfolk. The AWS seminar and exam schedule shows which sessions hold Part B.

faq.q: Which code book should a port crane or wharf welder choose?
faq.a: Usually AWS D1.1, 2020 edition, since crane, wharf and terminal steel is normally welded to D1.1 or the crane maker's specifications.

faq.q: I hold the Savannah Tech Welding and Joining diploma. How much experience do I need?
faq.a: A completed trade or vocational program usually puts you on the four-year line of the AWS table. AWS decides whether your program and jobs count, so document each employer and keep someone who can confirm it.

faq.q: Is there an AWS section in Savannah?
faq.a: Savannah Technical College has an AWS student chapter, the Southern Welders, which belongs to the AWS Atlanta Section. The section finder on aws.org shows the nearest section meetings.

faq.q: Can a Bryan County supplier run the course for its quality team?
faq.a: Yes. With the corporate format the six days are delivered at the supplier's facility, using its own parts and gauges. Each person applies to AWS and sits the exam individually.

faq.q: Does AWS endorse the Atlantis course?
faq.a: No. The course carries no AWS approval or endorsement, and Atlantis has no access to AWS examination content. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification.

faq.q: How do I request a quote from Savannah?
faq.a: Use the enquiry link on this page with the format, the number of candidates and the Part C book. You get a quote for the chosen format on request, and a reply within one business day.
